Unit 11: Advanced Networking

HL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

Who defends the network when you sleep?

This unit focuses on Architectural Abstraction and Proactive Defense. While SL covered basic connections, HL dives into the 'How'—specifically the orchestration of the TCP/IP Stack, the logic of Dynamic Routing, and active countermeasures like IDS and IPS.

You'll start by dissecting the 4-layer TCP/IP Model (Encapsulation). Then you'll explore enterprise architecture (Reverse Proxies), and finally, you'll learn how to secure it all with Intrusion Prevention Systems.

TCP/IP Stack (The Model)

The rules of the internet. Data is wrapped in envelopes (Headers) as it moves down.

  • Application: Data.
  • Transport: Segments (Reliability).
  • Network: Packets (Addressing).
  • Link/Physical: Frames (Hardware).
Server Architecture

How do big sites handle millions of users?

  • Proxy Server: Hides the Client (Anonymity).
  • Reverse Proxy: Hides the Server (Security & Load Balancing).
Dynamic Routing

The internet is self-healing.

  • Routing Table: A map of the network stored on the router.
  • Dynamic: If a cable is cut, the router automatically recalculates a new "Optimal Path" in seconds.
Active Defense (IDS/IPS)

Firewalls are just gates. We need guards.

  • IDS (Detection): The Alarm. Watches traffic and alerts admin.
  • IPS (Prevention): The Bouncer. Watches traffic and actively BLOCKS threats.
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
TCP/IP Model The conceptual model and set of communications protocols used in the Internet (4 Layers).
Encapsulation The process of adding headers/footers to data as it moves down the protocol stack.
PDU (Protocol Data Unit) The specific unit of data at a layer (Segment, Packet, Frame).
Reverse Proxy A server that sits in front of web servers and forwards client requests to those web servers (Load balancing/Security).
Dynamic Routing A process where routers automatically exchange information to update their routing tables to find the best path.
IDS (Intrusion Detection System) A device or software application that monitors a network or system for malicious activity or policy violations (Alerts only).
IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) A network security tool that continuously monitors network traffic for malicious activity and takes action to prevent it (Blocks).
